Statements: Only a few files are deposits. All deposits are branches. No branches is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not deposits.
II. No deposits is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are deposits. All deposits are branches. No branches is a cheques.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are branches.
II. Some deposits are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No files is a deposits. Some deposits are branches. All branches are cheques.
Conclusions:
I. All files are cheques.
II. Some cheques are deposits.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All files are cheques.
II. No deposits is a cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Q > P < T > X < R.
Conclusions: I. R ≥ T   II. T < R.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
secure banking growth = ze su vo
secure savings access = ze lu ka
banking savings digital = ni ka vo
growth access digital = ni su lu
secure banking digital = ze ni vo
What is the code for “banking”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: secure = ze, banking = vo, growth = su, savings = ka, access = lu, digital = ni.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 71 km east, turns left and walks 72 km, then turns left and walks 17 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 90. Net displacement is 54 km east and 72 km north. By Pythagoras, √(54² + 72²) = 90 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 22 km east, turns left and walks 16 km, then turns left and walks 10 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 47 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 17 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: E is the mother of B. A is the daughter of B. C is the father of B. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of B, and A is B’s daughter. Hence A is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of B. B is the mother of D. A is the father of E and B. How is E related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of D’s mother B. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of E. E is the father of F. A is the son of F. D is the sister of E. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of F, and F is A’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 43 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 10+3 = 13. Back rank = 43 − 13 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem: In a queue of 39 candidates, a candidate is 14th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 22. New front rank = 14+4 = 18. Back rank = 39 − 18 + 1 = 22.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2300 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4395.56. Recover each cost separately: 2300×100/125 + 2300×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 56 and 84 hours. An outlet empties it in 84 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 56. Net rate = 1/56 + 1/84 − 1/84 = 1/56. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 144 km in still water in 8 hours. If the stream flows at 5 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 52. Still-water speed = 18 km/h. Upstream speed = 18 − 5. Distance = speed × 4.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 8:7. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 5 months. A receives ₹115200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 157200. Profit ratio is 96:35. Each ratio unit = ₹1200. Total = 131 × 1200.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹28000 earns ₹4200 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30870. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 28000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 80 litres of pure milk. 16 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 51.2. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 80 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 17 people is 27 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. New total minus old total = (17+1)×(27+1) − 17×27 = 45.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 13 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+13)/(x+13) = 3/2 gives x = 13. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 130 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 9.29. Relative speed = (57.6 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 14 m/s. Time = 130/14.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 25%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3300. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. New quantity / old quantity = 100/125. Reduction percentage = 25/125 ×100.
